live_language_inventory.ui_language_pickers: the /search page source/target language radio+checkbox groups list only the 24 official EU codes plus la and mul; be and uk are not offered in the UI

api_contract.unsigned_policy: large volumes of unsigned queries that impact performance are not processed; a token is issued by the IATE Support & Development Team (iate@cdt.europa.eu)
api_contract.observed_rate_limiting: short bursts of ~130 small GETs followed by searches received empty responses; single spaced queries succeeded again after a pause
api_contract.user_agent_note: the edge rejects some non-browser client fingerprints (python urllib -> 403/empty); curl with an identified custom User-Agent worked for the same payloads

be_blocker.conclusion: Belarusian is listed in the language inventory but is not searchable via the public API and is not offered in the UI

uk_state.targets_uk: searches with targets ["uk"] return entries whose language sections contain no uk term entries (20 sampled entries over the benchmark: 0 uk sections)

uk_state.conclusion: Ukrainian exists as inventory metadata and in the entry-view URL template, but no public Ukrainian term content was reachable; consistent with uk=0 in the 2019 export

benchmark.method: POST /entries/_search source=en targets=[uk,de,es,fr,cs,sv] limit=3; top 2 entries fetched per term; raw JSON responses kept locally in git-ignored scratch; only quoted values recorded here

negative - police stop (de Anhaltung, es alto policial, cs legitimování policií) and industrial close-down; no media-transport sense
negative - ship catwalk (de Laufsteg, es pasarela) and pathologic gait (de Hahnentritt); no pedestrian walk sense

limitations: the anonymous public bulk export is a stale 2019-02-26 snapshot (file Last-Modified 2019-09-30); no refresh schedule is documented on the pages consulted
filtered per-language TBX/CSV exports exist but require an EU Login account (external guest user); no account was created per task constraints
a search-API token for larger volumes requires contacting iate@cdt.europa.eu; not requested
Belarusian search returns HTTP 403 on the public API both as source and as target; the cause (WAF rule vs backend policy) is not documented publicly
the public API/UI expose no Ukrainian term content despite the inventory listing uk; only inventory metadata was observed
entry-level domain codes are opaque hashes in the API; human-readable domain labels were not resolved (would require the domains/_tree inventory)
downloaded TBX/zip and raw API responses stayed in local git-ignored scratch; only quoted values and metadata are recorded in this manifest
follow_up_drafts: F1 - documented rejection of IATE as a source of UI strings for KUDY: be is blocked/unavailable (HTTP 403; absent from UI pickers and the 2019 export), uk has no public term content, and of the six EU-official locales only 1 of 10 benchmark UI terms matches the KUDY sense (download; purchase is a partial noun) with the rest in EU-jargon domains; G21.33 records the decision, no integration task

F2 - optional reference use for tourism terminology: when reviewing the sense of domain words (tourist guide, guided tour) a translation record may cite the IATE entry URL (https://iate.europa.eu/em-api/entries/{code}) as one reference for the six EU-official locales; consultation only, no copying (license boundary); depends on G21.27 record form

F3 - human decision if deeper IATE use is ever approved: creating an EU Login guest account unlocks filtered per-language TBX/CSV exports (kept 7 days, attribution "Download IATE, European Union, [year]"); this is a human account step, not an agent action

F4 - any bulk adoption of IATE terms must come from the downloadable file (the only channel whose license explicitly allows reproduction), never from API/widget/site results; the anonymous full-tbx is stale 2019, so a fresh filtered export via EU Login would be the only current licensed source
